Consideration of the University of Rhode Island Total Budget Request for FY 2027, and recommendation for approval to the URI Board of Trustees.
Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance Vice President Benson presented the Total Budget Request for FY27, noting that this request is brought to the Board annually.
Her presentation included comparisons to the FY26 enacted budget and the difference between the FY26 request and the FY26 enacted budget as a baseline for the FY27 request.
She noted that the enacted appropriation for FY26 was $115.3 Million (out of a total all-funds budget of $1.11 Billion).
For FY27, the appropriation request is $143.9 Million (out of a $1.16 Billion all-funds budget).
Details on the request can be found in the presentation linked here.

Vice President Benson discussed the assumptions for the development of the FY27 request, namely small increases in both undergraduate and graduate enrollment, a 3% across-the-board tuition increase (noting that the Board will officially approve any tuition change in February), and small increases to certain student fees (Fitness and Wellness Center Fee, Memorial Union Fee, and Building Fee).
She also noted challenges to enrollment including nearby state free/reduced tuition programs, the Hope and Promise scholarships in Rhode Island, the uncertainty of federal impacts on student aid, volatile interest rates, and the impact of the quality of URI housing on both recruitment efforts and yield.
Vice President Benson noted that the Current Service Level request includes funds for student aid, debt service, insurance rate increases, impacts to fringe benefit rates, and operating increases relative to new buildings on campus.

With reference to the Strategic Initiatives included in the request, Vice President Benson noted that this component included 10 new faculty members, 13 new Academic Advisors, and additional support for the Talent Development, National Guard, and Tribal Scholarship programs.
There are also funds for the development of a new merit scholarship, Anchor in Rhode Island, aimed at attracting the top students in the state, although development of this initiative is still ongoing.
In an additional slide, Vice President Benson showed how these requests align not only with the URI Strategic Plan, but also the State’s RI2030 Strategic Plan priorities.
Vice President Benson also discussed the state’s full-time equivalent (FTE) cap, noting that while student enrollment at URI has grown 19% over the last twenty years, the FTE cap has only increased 4%.
Responding to board member inquiry, Vice President Benson stated that URI is below its peers in terms of staffing in many of its support areas.
Board members encouraged continuing efforts to advocate to the state for an increase in the cap.

The Committee decided to vote on the FY27 Total Budget less the Anchor in Rhode Island scholarship, since it is still in development and may be discussed by the full Board at an upcoming meeting.
Chair Ownjazayeri called for a motion, and on a motion duly made by Armand Sabitoni, and seconded by Michael Fascitelli, it was VOTED: To recommend approval of the University’s FY2027 Total Budget Request, less the Anchor in Rhode Island scholarship, as presented in the enclosure.

A single contractor responded with a bid that was $1.2 million above the estimated cost.

During review of the project design, replacement of the roof was added.
The roof , which was installed in 2007 and is in poor condition, will be improved to better facilitate replacement of the roof-top mechanical equipment.
The project bid package review, addition of the roofing system , and escalation results in a project cost increase of $4.7 million for a total project cost of $10.0 million.
The bid package as now structured, along with posting the bid in the fall of 2025, will allow the entire project to be completed in a single summer (2026), which will result in less disruption to Dining Services.
Recommendation: I recommend that the Board of Trustees approve the updated Dining Facilities Improvement project (Hope Commons) budget of $10.0 million, with a construction timeframe during the summer of 2026.
